intervalCertificateMethods: Rational operations round outward at every step; constants have explicit series remainder bounds.
Cosine uses Taylor recurrence plus the Lagrange remainder; dilogarithm uses its positive interior series and geometric tail.

Positive Gamma values use recurrence and a convergent log-Gamma expansion with a geometric remainder; Euler constant is bracketed using harmonic sum/integral comparison. The expansion is equivalent to NIST DLMF5.7.E3 on the actual rational interval.

Equality to the preserved correct display is checked literally after harmless whitespace/natural-log normalization. For the two finite binomial families, independent finite sums additionally check the answer. Other original analytic proofs remain unchanged and were previously source-bound reviewed.

firstCheckerIssue: An initial internal cosine enclosure used separately rounded factorial coefficients, producing overly wide intervals. It was rejected before any patch artifact was emitted and replaced by a stable Taylor recurrence with the same rigorous remainder. This was a checker issue, not a source mathematical error.
